The draft is safe and handles the injury signs well. It refers Marisol to a sports physio this week and names the warning signs: lateral knee pain that starts at a set point in the run, gets worse on downhills and lingers on stairs. It cancels Wednesday's tempo and puts a 40-minute bike or pool session in its place. It also cuts the week sharply, to about 19 miles of easy flat running plus cross-training, down from 32 miles.

On Marisol's questions: it answers the tempo question directly with a no. On the IT band question it honestly declines to diagnose and sends her to a physio instead of guessing.

Each easy run has clear stop rules. Thursday only goes ahead if Tuesday was pain-free, and the long run is cut to 8 flat miles with walk breaks and a point to stop.

I took off a point because the plan still schedules 8 miles on Sunday, and 3 miles on Saturday, before anyone has assessed the knee. I would have made the long run depend on what the physio says or capped it lower. Some lines are also cut off ("Abort at the…", "otherwise…"), so a couple of days are not fully clear to run as written.

Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 30, 32, 35 mi
This week: 32 mi over 5 runs. Planned 36 mi, ran 32 mi.
Pain noted: Thu 2/10 (Outside of right knee tight on the last hill); Sat 1/10 (Knee a little tight before the run, fine during); Sun 4/10 (Outside of right knee, sharp on downhills from mile 7. Walked the last half mile.)
Body: "Right knee aches going down stairs today. Never had this before."
Feeling: "Worried about the knee."
Asks: "Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?"

Safety flag: See a sports physio about the right knee
Safety flag: Stop a run if sharp knee pain returns
